solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fissure’s opening in old path, naturally (2,6)

indicatorNotes.opening: the opening of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: the F goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old; a course is a path
first letter of Fissure

annotation.surface: A crack has appeared in an ancient track, as you would expect.
annotation.walkthrough: The F slips in just after the O, before COURSE. 'Naturally' at the end is the definition, as in 'naturally, I agreed'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both phrases mean 'as anyone would expect'.

entries.clue: Dismiss characters residing in your street (4)

indicatorNotes.characters residing in: the letters living inside a word, away from its ends

blocks.note: the inner letters of yOUr
ST is the usual abbreviation for street

annotation.surface: Someone wants to get rid of the people living on your road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters, not residents: only the inside of YOUR is used, and street is abbreviated as on a map.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean forcing someone out of a job or place.

entries.clue: Advise company a Parisian steals regularly (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
UN is French for a
the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of StEaLs

annotation.surface: Someone warns a firm that a Frenchman keeps pilfering from it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A Parisian' means the word 'a' as a Parisian would say it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean giving someone guidance on what to do.

entries.clue: Lamentable piece of bun for tuna tested (11)

indicatorNotes.piece of: the answer is only a piece of the words that follow

blocks.note: bUN FOR TUNA TEsted

annotation.surface: A sorry-looking bit of bread roll was tried out as a partner for tuna.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across four words, dropping only the B of bun and the end of tested.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adjectives describe something regrettable, to be deplored.

entries.clue: Like retiring chap admitting love of Polynesian country (6)

indicatorNotes.retiring: going back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: like and as are both used for comparison
a chap is a man
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

annotation.surface: A description of a shy fellow who loves an island nation in the Pacific.
annotation.walkthrough: Only 'Like' goes backwards; the chap takes the O inside to give MOAN. The definition is adjectival, like the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective for the island state of Samoa, which lies in Polynesia in the South Pacific.

entries.clue: Backing friends to strike (4)

indicatorNotes.Backing: going backwards, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: pals are friends

annotation.surface: Supporting one's friends in walking out on strike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing friends' sounds like supporting them; it is the word PALS turned round, and 'strike' is a verb, not a walkout.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean hitting someone, here with an open hand.

entries.clue: Boozer in vicinity of 50, a colonel, toppled over (5)

indicatorNotes.toppled over: in a down clue, something toppled over is upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: L is 50 in Roman numerals
kept as is
COL is the abbreviation for colonel

annotation.surface: A drunk near the age of fifty, a military officer, has fallen over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is a British word for a pub, not a drinker; the pub nearest your home is the one meant.
annotation.definitionFit: British usage: the nearby pub is named by the adjective for nearby, used as a noun.

entries.clue: Ripest bananas briefly acquire great reputation (8)

indicatorNotes.bananas: slang for crazy, so the letters go wild
indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: RIPEST rearranged
GET without its last letter

annotation.surface: The ripest bananas win acclaim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' is not fruit here but the anagram indicator, meaning mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: high standing earned by achievement.

entries.clue: Fully pack possessions (5)

blocks.note: a verb: cram a bag until it is full
a casual noun for belongings

annotation.surface: An instruction to cram all your belongings in.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is a verb and the second a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a verb for cramming full and a casual noun for belongings.

entries.clue: Head of museum restored relic, a wonder (7)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.restored: rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of Museum
RELIC and A rearranged

annotation.surface: A museum director has restored an old artefact to marvellous effect.
annotation.walkthrough: The A after the comma is part of the anagram fodder; the definition brings its own article in 'a wonder'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an extraordinary, apparently supernatural event.

entries.clue: Rotten back tooth starts to emit reeks and cause trouble (4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.Rotten: spoilt, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.starts to: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
first letters of Emit and Reeks

annotation.surface: A decaying molar is giving off a foul smell and causing problems.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rotten back tooth' reads as dental decay, but 'Rotten' only tells you to shuffle the letters of BACK TOOTH plus E and R.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: upsetting a settled situation, as a passenger shaking a small craft would.

entries.clue: Knight, one with right jousting weapon to pierce opening (3,8)

indicatorNotes.to pierce: one thing going through another sits inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
R is the abbreviation for right
the long spear used in jousting
a slot is an opening

annotation.surface: A knight on horseback drives his weapon through a gap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the start of a joust; it is the gap the weapon goes through, split after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the best-known knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

entries.clue: Small rodents turned up in coop, for example (8)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so reversed

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
mice are rodents
a coop or pen is an enclosure for animals

annotation.surface: Little mice have appeared in a chicken coop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like it marks coop as an instance of something; here 'for' is the link and 'example' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one item taken as typical of its kind.

entries.clue: Exercise running back and forth (4-2)

indicatorNotes.running back and forth: a word that reads the same either way

blocks.note: the word reads identically in both directions

annotation.surface: Doing shuttle runs as a workout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running back and forth' sounds like a training drill; it describes the answer itself, which spells the same in both directions.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: hanging from a bar and hauling your chin above it is a gym exercise.

entries.clue: Self-confident saint not right after wife leaves (6)

indicatorNotes.after: the second piece comes after the first
indicatorNotes.leaves: when the wife leaves she departs, so her letter W is dropped from the word

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
what is not right is wrong
W is the abbreviation for wife, removed

annotation.surface: A sure-of-himself holy man goes astray once his wife walks out.
annotation.walkthrough: The W taken out of WRONG is the wife who leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: sure of oneself, not easily shaken.

entries.clue: Lack of power to contain king’s fury (7)

indicatorNotes.to contain: one word holds another inside it

blocks.note: a power outage is a loss of electricity
R, for Latin rex, is king

annotation.surface: A king is furious about a power cut.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of king's is read as 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: violent anger at something shocking.

entries.clue: Swear from top of precipitous rock shelf (6)

indicatorNotes.top of: in a down clue, the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Precipitous
a ledge is a shelf of rock

annotation.surface: A climber curses from the top of a steep rock ledge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swear' looks like cursing; here it means to promise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to promise solemnly.

entries.clue: Reduction of temperature in dog with illness (11)

indicatorNotes.in: the T is set in between the other two pieces

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
T is the abbreviation for temperature
an ailment is an illness

annotation.surface: A sick dog's fever is coming down.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a vet's report on a feverish dog; 'in' only places the T between the two words, not inside either.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the act of cutting something short.

entries.clue: Removing covers, Irish gent is out of bed (5)

indicatorNotes.Removing covers: the covers of a word are its outer letters, taken away

blocks.note: IRISH without its first and last letters
GENT without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Throwing off the bedclothes, an Irishman gets up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Removing covers' paints someone throwing off blankets; it strips the outer letters from both Irish and gent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having got up in the morning.

entries.clue: Cycling bearing hot drinks (4)

indicatorNotes.Cycling: moving letters round from one end to the other

blocks.note: east is a compass bearing; its last letter moves to the front

annotation.surface: Taking cups of tea along on a bike ride.
annotation.walkthrough: Move the T of EAST from the back to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cups of the brewed leaf are one kind of hot drink.

entries.clue: Bungling males I’d deceive (7)

indicatorNotes.Bungling: handled clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Someone admits they would trick clumsy men.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I'd is ignored: the fodder is just the letters I and D.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: leading someone into a false belief.

entries.clue: Lecture’s nothing to value (5)

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
to rate is to value

annotation.surface: A talk is judged worthless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecture's' is 'Lecture is', a verb joined to its wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to speak at length in a formal, pompous way.

entries.clue: Reportedly negative to German figure (4)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: what is reported is heard, so we go by sound

blocks.note: nein is German for no

annotation.surface: Apparently a German keeps saying no to a number.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' means a number here, not a shape or a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: figure means a number, here the one after eight.

entries.clue: Reversing bit of dissent, federation shows skill (8)

indicatorNotes.Reversing: going backwards, so the letters are turned round
indicatorNotes.bit of: only part of the word is used

blocks.note: the last five letters of diSSENT
FED is short for federation

annotation.surface: Backing down on a disagreement, a federation proves adept.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' sounds like backing down in an argument, but it turns round both pieces together, so the federation ends up in front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: neat, quick dexterity, especially with the hands.
